pages.text: The mech is a suit of armour you pilot, about three and a half blocks tall. You climb into its trunk, and it walks, jumps, digs and punches for you while its armour takes the hits. It is end-game: its heart is a crystal grown from reactor waste.

It wears teal armour with mint enamel and steel trim: a broad chest that comes to a prow, big angular shoulders, a steel V crest on its brow and two thrusters on its back. Its trunk is a bay you stand in, back against a harness, looking out through the visor of its head.

$(li)A $(l:mech/mech_core)Mech Core$(/l), built around a Fusion Crystal from the $(l:mech/crystallizer)Crystallizer$(/l).$(br)$(li)The $(item)Mech Frame$(), crafted around the Mech Core.$(br)$(li)A $(l:mech/mech_hangar)Mech Hangar$(/l): a frame only unfolds on a hangar's pad.$(br)$(li)Optional: $(l:mech/mech_modules)Mech Modules$(/l) for flight, a drill, a blade and armour.
pages.title: What you need

pages.text: Right-click the hangar's pad with the Mech Frame. The mech unfolds in the middle of the pad, facing out of the hangar. A new frame comes with $(l)200,000 FE$() in its battery.
pages.title: Standing it up

pages.text: To pack it up again, park it on the pad and press $(l)Fold$() on the hangar's console. It folds itself up and drops as its frame, keeping the battery's charge and its modules.

$(li)$(l)Right-click$() the mech to get in. It crouches with its knees apart and its front opens: the two chest plates swing apart like a book, the two abdomen doors swing aside after them, and the visor plate lifts with the crest on it. You walk up between its knees, turn round
pages.title: Getting in and out

pages.text: $(li)and back into the bay, up a step. The plates close around you and the mech straightens up.$(br)$(li)$(l)Press V$() (the $(o)Exit mech$() key in the controls) to get out. It crouches and opens with a hiss of steam, you step down out of the bay and walk off, and it closes up again.

$(li)$(l)W A S D$(): Walk; turn by looking around$(br)$(li)$(l)Space$(): Jump about five blocks high$(br)$(li)$(l)Left click (empty hand)$(): Punch: 10 extra damage, 100 FE$(br)$(li)$(l)Left click a block$(): Dig like an iron pickaxe, with the right drops
pages.title: Piloting

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Space in the air (Jet module)$(): Climb; sneak to dive, neither to glide$(br)$(li)$(l)R / G (Drill / Blade module)$(): Switch the drill or the blade on and off$(br)$(li)$(l)V$(): Get out$(br)$(li)$(l)F5$(): Outside view, from further back$(br)The keys are in the controls under $(o)CyberFarm Mech$().

$(li)The pilot reaches $(l)2.5 blocks$() further from the cockpit. The crosshair never lands on the mech itself.$(br)$(li)Inside, you are shielded: whatever would hurt you hurts the mech instead. Neither of you takes fall damage.
$(li)In first person you look out through the visor. The mech's arms are at your sides and throw a punch when you hit, and looking down you see its legs.

$(l)Integrity$() is the mech's health. It never blows up: when it would, it $(l)shuts down$(). Its lights go out, it slumps over and lets you out. A shut-down mech must be repaired before you can climb in again.$(br2)With an empty battery the mech cannot move, but you can still get out.
pages.title: Battery and integrity

pages.text: Park it in a $(l:mech/mech_hangar)Mech Hangar$(/l) to charge its battery, repair it and fit its $(l:mech/mech_modules)modules$(/l).$(br)$(li)$(l)Battery$(): 1,000,000 FE$(br)$(li)$(l)Charge of a new frame$(): 200,000 FE$(br)$(li)$(l)Walking$(): about 200 FE per block$(br)$(li)$(l)Systems, while you sit inside$(): 2 FE/t$(br)$(li)$(l)Punch$(): 100 FE$(br)$(li)$(l)Integrity$(): 200

While you pilot, the usual hearts, hunger and experience bar give way to the mech's display. When the cockpit closes, the systems boot with a scan of the view. Then you see:$(br)$(li)brackets in the corners and a reticle around the crosshair;
pages.title: The cockpit display

pages.text: $(li)a $(l)compass$() along the top, with your heading in degrees;$(br)$(li)$(l)ENERGY$() and $(l)INTEGRITY$() bars on the left, flashing a warning when power runs low;$(br)$(li)$(l)speed$(), $(l)altitude$() and the installed $(l)modules$() on the right.
You hear it, too: servos and a hiss of steam as it opens, the armour locking shut, the systems booting, heavy footsteps and a thud when it lands, the jet's roar, the drill's spin and the blade's hum.
